metadata.case_name: BUAPHAN WANLAYAPHOL AND ANOTHER v. THE INCORPORATED OWNERS OF THE FOREMOST BUILDING

injuries.description: right acute subdural haematoma and high parietal depressed skull fracture; 13 cm laceration on the right scalp; comatose on admission (Glasgow coma scale 3/15).
source: the deceased was comatose on admission (Glasgow coma scale 3/15) with a 13 cm laceration on the right scalp. Urgent CT brain scan was conducted, revealing a right acute subdural haematoma and high parietal depressed skull fracture.

injuries.description: extensive brain damage causing severe disability, leading to profound cognitive and motor impairment, incontinence and dependence on others; expected to be wheelchair bound for life.
source: He was satisfied that the deceased's extensive brain damage would cause severe disability requiring years of rehabilitation.
injuries.icd_description: Diffuse injury of multiple parts of brain

injuries.description: one ½ inch laceration, a 2 ½ inch laceration and an abrasion wound over the parietal-occipital region of the scalp (2nd plaintiff).
source: the 2nd plaintiff had sustained a one ½ inch laceration, a 2 ½ inch laceration and an abrasion wound over the parietal-occipital region of the scalp. There was no skull fracture or any history of loss of consciousness.

manifestations.description: 13 cm laceration on the right scalp
unable to speak, eat or drink and had to be fed artificially
increased muscle tone in the extremities, but decreased muscle tone in the trunk
clonus in the wrists and short adductors and flexors at the hip
spasticity in both the upper and lower extremities and flexion contractures especially in the right arm at the shoulder and elbow and in both legs
general hypertonus and rigidity in the muscles, and difficulty in activating reflexes; right side Babinski positive
marginal cognition; little or no meaningful communication; 'yes' and 'no' expressed non-verbally; little voluntary muscle control; could sit in a wheelchair and move body forward
frequent chest infection and increasing susceptibility to opportunistic infections (leading to eventual death from suppurative bronchitis)
occasional dizziness, headaches and neck pain; pain and stiffness in the neck; occasional pain in the right leg and sensation of loss of strength in the right arm (2nd plaintiff)

reactive depression, mood swings, moderate signs of depression and reduced minor cognitive abilities (assessed at 10% under Swedish Insurance Federation guidelines); psychosomatic illness, sleep disturbance, anxiety (2nd plaintiff)
fatigue and reduced ability to work; episodes of crying several times a week (2nd plaintiff)

losses.description: Pain, suffering and loss of amenities of the deceased (PSLA) awarded HK$1,000,000.
Loss of motor function assessed at 95%; expected to be wheelchair bound for the rest of her life.
Wholly dependent upon others for all her daily needs; required 24-hour care.
Unable to speak; could not communicate meaningfully in Swedish; 'yes' and 'no' expressed non-verbally.

losses.category: Loss of ability to do domestic tasks
losses.description: Unable to perform ordinary household activities; required husband and hired helpers for all daily needs and home adaptation.
2nd plaintiff: depression, reduced minor cognitive abilities, mood swings and other psychiatric sequelae for which HK$600,000 awarded.
2nd plaintiff forced to retire early and stop working as a chef; loss of earnings and pension diminution awarded.
